Scientific posters from Python: a layout of text, figures and equations written to a
print-ready PDF. A poster is a title, the authors and blocks of text and figures in columns;
text, titles and captions are LaTeX, and the poster is a
[tikzposter](https://ctan.org/pkg/tikzposter) file compiled with lualatex.

Documentation: <https://max-models.github.io/plasma-posters/>

## Install

```bash
pip install plasma-posters
```

Compiling needs a TeX distribution with `lualatex` and the tikzposter class (TeX Live, MacTeX
or MiKTeX).

## A first poster

```python
from plasma_posters import Poster

poster = Poster(
    "Speeds in a thermal plasma",
    authors="Max Lindqvist",
    institute="Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics",
    columns=2,
)
poster.block("The distribution", r"$f(v) \propto v^2 \exp(-m v^2 / 2 k_B T)$")
poster.figure(
    "Three temperatures", "maxwellian.pdf", caption="Normalised to its peak.", column=1
)
poster.build("poster.pdf")  # writes poster.tex next to it and compiles it
```

A `.tex` written with `poster.save("poster.tex")` and edited by hand is compiled with
`plasma-posters build poster.tex`.

## Development

With [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/):

```bash
make install    # uv sync --extra dev, plus the pre-commit hooks
make lint       # ruff check, ruff format --check, ssort, pyright
make test       # pytest with coverage
```

## Build docs

The documentation in `docs/` is an Astro + Starlight site with the shared
[starlight-theme](https://github.com/max-models/starlight-theme): hand-written pages, the
notebooks in `tutorials/` executed and published as pages, the scripts in `examples/` with
their figures, and the API reference generated from the docstrings. It needs Node 22 or newer.

```bash
make docs-install     # npm packages and the Python docs extra
make docs-notebooks   # execute tutorials/*.ipynb and convert them to pages
make docs-dev         # live preview at http://localhost:4321/plasma-posters/
make docs-build       # the static site in docs/dist
```

## Releases

Before merging a release to `main`, update the version in `pyproject.toml` and add the release
notes to `CHANGELOG.md`. The push to `main` creates a GitHub release with a `vX.Y.Z` tag and
publishes the package to PyPI with trusted publishing; the one-time setup is described in the
[publishing guide](https://max-models.github.io/plasma-posters/development/publishing/).
